name: ExamLens AI
short_description: Analyzes past exam papers with an LLM to surface likely topics, predict questions, and generate a study roadmap.
problem: Before exams, students often work from a stack of previous question papers with no systematic way to see which topics repeat, which are likely to appear again, or how to prioritize limited revision time.
solution: ExamLens AI ingests past exam papers and uses an LLM to analyze question patterns across years. It surfaces a topic heatmap, predicts likely upcoming questions, generates a personalized study roadmap, extracts key formulas, and produces practice MCQs — all exportable as a PDF report.
features: Topic heatmap across multiple years of papers
Predicted questions for the next exam
One-click PDF export of the analysis
engineering_decisions: Chose Streamlit for the interface to move quickly from analysis logic to a usable tool without building a separate frontend.
Used Groq's hosted Llama 3.3 for inference speed, given the interactive, multi-step nature of the analysis.

name: Smart Campus Sustainability Dashboard
tagline: A live sustainability dashboard for PSIT Kanpur.
short_description: Tracks energy, water, and solar usage by department, with anomaly detection, forecasting, and a Green Score.
problem: Campus facilities teams and departments had no consolidated, real-time view of energy, water, and solar performance — making it hard to spot waste, anomalies, or track sustainability progress over time.
solution: A dashboard that ingests campus utility data and applies three ML models: Isolation Forest for anomaly detection on consumption patterns, Prophet for forecasting future usage, and a Decision Tree for predicting a department-level Green Score. Results are surfaced through monitoring views, a department leaderboard, and estimated CO₂ savings.
engineering_decisions: Used three purpose-built models (Isolation Forest, Prophet, Decision Tree) instead of one general model, since anomaly detection, time-series forecasting, and score prediction are distinct problems with different data assumptions.

name: PathForge
short_description: An AI-powered career intelligence system that analyzes skills and job requirements to identify career gaps and prioritize skills for development.
problem: Job seekers often know their current skills but lack a structured way to compare those skills with changing job requirements and identify which skills would have the greatest impact on their career direction.
solution: PathForge analyzes resume and profile information, converts skills into structured representations, retrieves relevant job requirements using semantic similarity, and compares current skills with required skills to identify prioritized career gaps.
architecture: Resume/profile → NLP skill extraction → structured skill profile → semantic retrieval of job postings → required skill representation → skill-gap comparison → career resilience analysis → prioritized recommendations.
engineering_decisions: Used Sentence Transformers for semantic representations instead of relying only on keyword matching.
Used FAISS for efficient similarity search over job and skill representations.
Used DuckDB for analytical processing of job-posting data.
Designed the system around structured skill comparison so recommendations are grounded in identifiable career gaps.
